audit.whatIsWrong: Devour is repeatedly called a W — "the W Devour now has a target" (whys[4]) and "your W Devour is the only button that stops it" (spikes[3].text).
audit.why: Devour is Tahm Kench's R. His W is Abyssal Dive, a 1000-1200 range knockup on 21/20/19/18/17s. In a matchup whose entire late-game plan is written around swallowing Wukong, telling the player it is on W points them at the wrong button at the one moment that decides the fight.
audit.corrected: Devour is the R. Abyssal Dive is the W.

audit.whatIsWrong: The late-game plan — "track him the moment R begins spinning and Devour him instantly" — never mentions that Devour requires three An Acquired Taste stacks on the target first.
audit.why: This is the load-bearing omission in the matchup. Riot's passive text: "At three stacks, he can use Devour on an enemy champion." A Tahm Kench who walks into a teamfight with zero stacks on Wukong has a greyed-out ultimate the instant Cyclone starts, which is precisely the scenario the text tells him to plan for. The requirement is to chip Wukong BEFORE the fight, not to react to the ult.
audit.corrected: Devour is gated on three stacks. Land chip damage on Wukong before the fight starts or the button is unavailable when Cyclone goes off.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json (Riot Data Dragon 16.15.1) — An Acquired Taste

audit.whatIsWrong: content.mid, content.whys[4] and content.spikes[1].text tell the player "Abyssal Voyage makes you a global threat" / "adds global threat" at level 6, and sell a "stun-into-Devour" combo.
audit.why: Abyssal Voyage is the removed pre-2020 W; there is no global ability in the kit. And the three stacks are one shared charge: Riot's Q text says at 3 stacks "they are stunned and the stacks are consumed", while the passive says 3 stacks are what allows Devour. The Q stun leaves the ultimate uncastable — fatal in the exact scenario this matchup is built around.
audit.corrected: Level 6 gives Devour, not map presence. Three stacks buys the stun OR Devour; against Wukong it must be Devour.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.you[0] and dosFull[1] both correctly say to wait for the W clone, but neither gives the cooldown, and breakdown.cooldowns points at Nimbus Strike with no number at all.
audit.why: Warrior Trickster is the longest cooldown in Wukong's laning kit at 22/21/20/19/18s — far longer than Nimbus Strike's 10/9.25/8.5/7.75/7s or Crushing Blow's 8/7.5/7/6.5/6s. That 22-second gap at rank 1 is the actual window where Tahm Kench can land three stacks on a target who cannot vanish, and it is the number the whole matchup plan hinges on.
audit.corrected: Warrior Trickster 22/21/20/19/18s is the window. Nimbus Strike 10s, Crushing Blow 8s, Cyclone 130/110/90s.

audit.why: 47.69% over 1080 games with Wukong taking 5 of 7 stages, diff TRICKY at 7.5/10. The chart, the rating and the number all agree that Tahm Kench is behind — this one is internally consistent and needed no reconciliation.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[3].text and whys[6] claim Devour "is the only button that stops it mid-channel" and "the only ability in the game that removes a spinning Cyclone".
audit.why: Cyclone carries no channel flag in the kit and Riot's text does not describe it as interruptible, so whether Devour cuts it short is not answerable from the data on disk — and per the brief this is exactly the class of claim (suppression vs channel behaviour) that must be verified on the Wiki or left alone. I have removed the unverifiable superlative and replaced it with the stack-gate fact, which IS in the kit and is more actionable anyway.
audit.corrected: Dropped the "only button / stops it mid-channel" claim; kept the verifiable requirement that Devour needs three stacks banked before Cyclone launches.
sources: champ-data/_kits/monkeyking.json — Cyclone has no channel flag

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are genuinely his window — he has the full E-Q-W-auto loop, your armor is shredded, and your only real threat (the 3-stack stun) requires him to stand still long enough for you to hit him three times, which he simply will not do. Hold your Tongue Lash as a deterrent, not a trade opener; if you miss it he gap-closes for free. At level 6 the dynamic shifts: Abyssal Voyage makes you a global threat and, more importantly, you now have the presence of mind to let him use W first. Watch for the clone — when the real Wukong reappears to all-in, you already have stacks queued and the stun-into-Devour timing punishes him exactly when his decoy is on cooldown and he is committed.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are genuinely his window — he has the full E-Q-W-auto loop, your armor is shredded, and your only real threat (three An Acquired Taste stacks) requires him to stand still long enough for you to hit him three times, which he simply will not do. Hold your Tongue Lash as a deterrent, not a trade opener; if you miss it he gap-closes for free. At level 6 the dynamic shifts: Devour arrives and, more importantly, you now have the presence of mind to let him use W first. Warrior Trickster is 22s at rank 1 — when the real Wukong reappears with the clone spent, put your three stacks into Devour, not the Q stun, because the stun consumes them.

edits.before: You will not solo-kill Wukong in extended 1v1s — his armor stacking and Trinity Force burst mean the damage race does not favor you. Your late-game job is entirely about Cyclone. In every team fight, track him the moment R begins spinning and Devour him instantly; removing a spinning Wukong from the fight is the single highest-value play you can make. If you are not in position to swallow him, position between him and your carries so his knockup hits you instead of them. You scale into a near-unkillable disruptor, but this lane is decided by how well you deny his R, not by winning the 1v1.
edits.after: You will not solo-kill Wukong in extended 1v1s — his Stone Skin armor stacking and Trinity Force burst mean the damage race does not favor you. Devour is gated on three An Acquired Taste stacks, so you have to chip him BEFORE the fight opens — arriving with zero stacks means your ultimate is greyed out at the exact moment it matters. If you cannot swallow him, position between him and your carries so his knockup hits you instead of them. You scale into a near-unkillable disruptor, but this lane is decided by how well you deny his R, not by winning the 1v1.

notes: The packet reports 0 defects and 0 suspectNames for this matchup, but it contains the worst single error in my slice: Devour is called a W twice, in the two lines that carry the entire late-game plan. A name-distance detector cannot catch a correct ability name attached to the wrong slot letter — worth adding a slot-vs-name cross-check to the validator. Separately, spikes[3].text and whys[6] asserted that Devour stops Cyclone "mid-channel" and is "the only ability in the game" that does; Cyclone has no channel flag in the kit and Riot's text does not describe it as interruptible, so I removed the claim rather than restate it. If someone verifies the Cyclone/suppression interaction on the League Wiki it can go back in with a citation.
